title: Digital Image and Video Processing
description: A comprehensive introduction to two-dimensional signals and systems, image enhancement, restoration, compression standards (JPEG, MPEG), and morphological processing. Includes programming assignments on real-world visual media.
prerequisites: CS 229 or STATS 214; linear algebra, multivariate calculus

title: Multimedia Security & Digital Watermarking
description: Advanced graduate course on the theory and implementation of digital watermarking, steganography, steganalysis, and copy-move forgery detection. Explores vulnerabilities in compressed domains (H.264, HEVC) and AI-generated media.
format: 3 Policy Position Papers + Final Capstone Case

title: Advanced Computer Vision
description: Deep convolutional architectures for action recognition, object detection, and semantic segmentation in video sequences.

title: Signals and Systems
description: Continuous and discrete-time signals, Fourier analysis, Laplace transforms, and linear time-invariant systems.

title: Quality Assessment of Digital Media
description: Seminar on subjective and objective metrics (PSNR, SSIM, VMAF) for image and video quality evaluation, including perceptual models.
